minutes.headline: Assessors voted to put two veterans-exemption articles, clauses 22I and 22J, on the November 17 town meeting warrant.
minutes.summary: The board approved two sets of executive session minutes, then reviewed classification hearing preparations. The commercial and industrial valuations from Vision are a month late, and the hearing date is tight. It then voted separately to submit two Hero Act warrant articles, one tying veterans exemptions to inflation and one roughly doubling them. Town counsel may still change the wording or require staggering.

votes.motion: Approve the September 9th executive session minutes as amended, changing 'veterans exception' to 'hardship'.
Accept the September 23rd executive session minutes as written, for release.
Put the warrant article for clause 22I (CPI-tied veterans exemption increase) on the town warrant as written.
Put the warrant article for clause 22J (doubling veterans exemptions) on the town warrant.

A board member illustrated doubling the base amount and then applying a CPI increase.

decisions.decision: If the two articles cannot both be adopted in the same year, the board would prefer to propose the doubling article (22J) first.
The chair will check with town counsel on whether both articles can run in the same year.
A board member will prepare the potential tax impact figures and send the final draft to the town manager.
Pending exemption applications are deferred to the October 14th agenda.
The board prefers a Nov 24 classification hearing over Dec 1, and will press Vision for the commercial and industrial data.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to place two veterans-exemption articles, clauses 22I and 22J, on the town meeting warrant; the tally was not audible.
Clause 22I ties the veterans exemption increase to inflation (CPI); clause 22J would double the exemptions. The board voted on each separately.
If town counsel says both cannot be adopted in the same year, the board would propose the doubling article (22J) first; the chair will ask counsel.
The board noted the cost of the exemptions falls on the town with no state reimbursement; a member will prepare tax impact figures for the town manager.
The board prefers a Nov 24 classification hearing over Dec 1 and will press Vision for the commercial and industrial data, which is late.

why_it_matters: If town meeting adopts either article, the exemption cost is shifted onto other taxpayers' bills, because the state does not reimburse it.
The late commercial and industrial valuations could squeeze the classification hearing, which sets how the tax burden is split between homes and businesses.
